tamil_fresh_a.role: the preprint's language, first list built afresh by the lab's prompts
tamil_fresh_a.CORPUS: the Sangam poems and the Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions
tamil_fresh_a.REFERENCE: the Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras), the Dravidian Etymological Dictionary and indexes of names in the Sangam poems and the Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions
tamil_fresh_a.ROMANISATION: the transliteration of the Tamil Lexicon and the Dravidian Etymological Dictionary (ā ī ū ē ō, ṅ ñ ṇ ṉ, ṭ ṟ, ḷ ḻ)

tamil_fresh_b.role: the preprint's language, second list built afresh, by other sessions
tamil_fresh_b.CORPUS: the Sangam poems and the Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions
tamil_fresh_b.REFERENCE: the Tamil Lexicon (University of Madras), the Dravidian Etymological Dictionary and indexes of names in the Sangam poems and the Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions
tamil_fresh_b.ROMANISATION: the transliteration of the Tamil Lexicon and the Dravidian Etymological Dictionary (ā ī ū ē ō, ṅ ñ ṇ ṉ, ṭ ṟ, ḷ ḻ)

japanese.role: control; the language of the public rebuttal
japanese.CORPUS: the Kojiki, the Nihon shoki and the Man'yōshū
japanese.REFERENCE: indexes of names in the Kojiki, Nihon shoki and Man'yōshū and dictionaries of Old Japanese (for example the Jidaibetsu kokugo daijiten and the Oxford-NINJAL Corpus of Old Japanese)
japanese.ROMANISATION: modified Hepburn romanisation of the traditional reading, with long vowels marked by a macron (ō ū), without the special vowel distinctions of reconstructed Old Japanese

greek.LANGUAGE: Ancient Greek (the Greek of Homer and Hesiod)
greek.CORPUS: the Iliad, the Odyssey, and Hesiod's Theogony and Works and Days
greek.REFERENCE: Liddell-Scott-Jones, the Lexicon of Greek Personal Names, and indexes of names in Homer and Hesiod
greek.LOANS: no words known to be borrowed from non-Greek languages
greek.ROMANISATION: scholarly transliteration without accents: ē and ō for eta and omega, ph th kh for the aspirates, y for upsilon, h for the rough breathing

old_english.CORPUS: texts written before 1100: Beowulf and the other Old English poems, the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, Bede, and the Anglo-Saxon charters
old_english.REFERENCE: Bosworth-Toller, the Dictionary of Old English, the Prosopography of Anglo-Saxon England and Searle's Onomasticon Anglo-Saxonicum
old_english.LOANS: no Latin, Celtic or Norse loans
old_english.ROMANISATION: the normal edited spelling (æ, þ, ð kept), with long vowels marked by a macron

hebrew.REFERENCE: Brown-Driver-Briggs, HALOT and standard dictionaries of biblical names
hebrew.LOANS: no Egyptian, Akkadian, Persian or other non-Semitic loans
hebrew.ROMANISATION: a plain scholarly transliteration: š for shin, ś for sin, ṣ for tsade, ṭ for tet, ḥ for chet, q for qof, ʾ and ʿ for aleph and ayin, long vowels with a macron, no marks for soft b g d k p t

nahuatl.CORPUS: sixteenth-century sources: the Florentine Codex, the Codex Mendoza and the early annals and histories
nahuatl.REFERENCE: Molina's Vocabulario, Karttunen's Analytical Dictionary of Nahuatl, and studies of Nahuatl personal and place names
nahuatl.ROMANISATION: the standard classical spelling (c, qu, hu, tl, tz, ch, x, z), with long vowels marked by a macron where known and the saltillo written h

sumerian.CORPUS: texts of the third millennium BCE (Early Dynastic, Old Akkadian and Ur III periods)
sumerian.REFERENCE: the Electronic Pennsylvania Sumerian Dictionary, the Cuneiform Digital Library and standard studies of Sumerian personal names
sumerian.ROMANISATION: normalised transliteration as running words, without sign index numbers, hyphens or dots (š, ḫ and ĝ kept)

hawaiian.CORPUS: traditional sources recorded in the nineteenth century: the Kumulipo, the chiefly genealogies, the traditions collected by Fornander, Kamakau and Malo, and traditional place names
hawaiian.REFERENCE: the Hawaiian Dictionary of Pukui and Elbert and Place Names of Hawaii by Pukui, Elbert and Mookini
hawaiian.LOANS: no English or other introduced loans
hawaiian.ROMANISATION: modern Hawaiian spelling, with the ʻokina (ʻ) and long vowels marked by a macron

finnish.role: control; also run by both parties to the dispute
finnish.CORPUS: the Kalevala and the Kanteletar, and old native Finnish personal and place names recorded in medieval and early modern documents
finnish.REFERENCE: the Suomen sanojen alkuperä etymological dictionary, the Kalevala and its name indexes, and standard studies of old Finnish personal names and place names
finnish.LOANS: no Swedish, Germanic, Baltic, Slavic or other borrowed words where the borrowing is well established and later than Proto-Finnic
